# What to Know About Ted Turner's 3 Ex-Wives, Including Actress Jane Fonda
### NEED TO KNOW
*   CNN founder Ted Turner was married three times to Julia Nye, Jane Shirley Smith and actress Jane Fonda  
*   He welcomed two children with Nye and three children with Smith  
*   Turner died on May 6 at age 87
Ted Turner, who died at age 87 on May 6, was married three times during his life.
The CNN founder wed Julia Gale Nye in 1960. The couple went on to welcome two children, daughter Laura and son Robert "Teddy" Edward IV,before divorcing after just a few years of marriage.
In 1964, Turner married Jane Shirley Smith. The pair, who eventually split in 1988, welcomed three children, Beau, Rhett and Jennie.
The media mogul's final marriage was to actress Jane Fonda from 1991 to 2001. During an interview with Piers Morgan in 2012, Turner admitted that Fonda was "probably" the great love of his life.
"When you love somebody, and you really love them, you never stop loving them," the media mogul added. "There's nothing wrong with that. That's good."
Here's everything to know about Ted Turner's ex-wives: Julia Gale Nye, Jane Shirley Smith and Jane Fonda.

# What to Know About Ted Turner's 3 Ex-Wives, Including Actress Jane Fonda
## Julia Gale Nye
Ted Turner.  
Bettmann/Getty
Julia Gale Nye, the daughter of world champion sailor Harry Gale Nye Jr., met Ted Turner while he was attending Brown University in 1959. The couple married at St. Chrysostom’s Episcopal Church in Chicago on June 22, 1960, according to the _Chicago Tribune_.
They later welcomed a daughter, Laura, in 1961, and a son, Robert Edward IV, in 1963, before going their separate ways, per Michael O'Connor's book _Ted Turner: A Biography_.

# What to Know About Ted Turner's 3 Ex-Wives, Including Actress Jane Fonda
## Jane Shirley Smith
Ted Turner attends official CNN Launch event on June 01, 1980 in Atlanta, Georgia.  
Rick Diamond/Getty
Shortly after his divorce from Nye, Turner married Jane Shirley Smith on June 2, 1964. Smith, a Delta Air Lines flight attendant, reportedly met Turner at a Young Republicans meeting.
The couple welcomed three children together: son Rhett in 1965 — named after Rhett Butler from _Gone with the Wind_ — followed by son Beau in 1968 and daughter Sarah Jean “Jennie” in 1969.
Turner and Smith divorced in 1988.

Ted Turner, the billionaire media mogul who founded CNN and helped reshape modern television, died Wednesday, at age 87.
Over decades, Turner built a vast empire that included cable networks such as TBS and TNT, while also leaving a lasting mark on professional sports through his ownership of the Atlanta Braves.
Known for his bold personality and willingness to take risks, he transformed both the way news is delivered—launching the first 24-hour cable news channel—and how sports teams could be marketed to a national audience. His larger-than-life persona, as well as his marriages to high-profile figures including actor Jane Fonda, cemented his place as one of the most recognizable media figures of his era.

#### Read More on U.S.
He was married three times throughout his life—to Julia Gale Nye, Jane Shirley Smith and Jane Fonda—and had five children across those relationships.
Jane Fonda peers out from under a towel shielding her from the rain as she and her husband, Ted Turner, watch the Atlanta Braves defeat the Pittsburgh...
Fonda paid tribute to Turner with a deeply personal reflection, describing him as a transformative presence in her life who brought both passion and support.
In a statement, Fonda recalled how Turner “swept into my life, a gloriously handsome, deeply romantic” figure whose larger-than-life persona was matched by his accomplishments as the founder of CNN and Turner Classic Movies and his success as a world-class sailor.
Fonda said he “could see around corners” and credited him with teaching her about wildlife conservation, as well as broader lessons in business and life. His competitive nature, she added, was among his defining traits, comparing it to that of legendary actor Katharine Hepburn.
She also pointed to Turner’s influence beyond his personal relationships, recalling how he challenged those around him to “think big and act small,” including encouraging ambitious ideas like banning nuclear weapons while embracing everyday acts such as picking up trash.
Fonda reflected on Turner’s environmental legacy, saying she imagines him reunited “with all the wildlife he helped bring back from extinction,” including bison, wolves and other species. She also acknowledged his five children, describing them as “talented, complex” individuals and noting the challenges and pride that came with being part of his extended family.
“I loved Ted with all my heart,” Fonda said, closing her tribute by honoring his lasting impact and memory: “You are loved and you will be remembered.”

## Ted Turner's First Wife, Julia Gale Nye
Turner married his first wife, Nye, in 1960. The marriage ended in divorce in 1964. Together, they had two children.
Nye largely stayed out of the public spotlight, even as Turner’s media career accelerated in the following decades. The relationship came during his early years in business, before he built the broadcasting empire that would later make him a household name.

## Ted Turner's Second Wife, Jane Shirley Smith
Turner married Smith in 1965, beginning a relationship that would last more than two decades. The couple divorced in 1988.
They had three children together. During this period, Turner was expanding his television holdings and taking increasingly high-profile risks across sports and media, including acquiring the Atlanta Braves and building out his cable networks.
Ted Turner and Jane Fonda are shown in this 1990 file photo. (AP Images)

## Ted Turner and Jane Fonda: What We Know
Turner’s most high-profile marriage was to actor and activist Fonda, whom he married in 1991. The relationship drew widespread attention given their celebrity status and influence in different fields, with the pairing bringing together two of the most recognizable public figures of the era.
The couple remained married for about a decade before divorcing in 2001, and they did not have children together. Their relationship played out largely in the public eye during a period when Turner’s media empire was expanding and Fonda was continuing her work in film and activism, keeping both figures firmly in the spotlight.
Their marriage also reflected a broader mix of personalities and priorities that defined both of their careers. Turner, known for his outspoken and often unpredictable style, contrasted with Fonda’s evolving focus on activism and spirituality, dynamics that were often noted in coverage of their relationship.
Even after their divorce, the relationship remained a defining part of Turner’s personal life. He later spoke publicly about the significance of the marriage, describing Fonda as one of the most important relationships he had—underscoring how closely his personal life and public profile were intertwined during that period.

## Ted Turner's Kids
Turner had five children across his first two marriages: Laura Turner Seydel, Robert Edward Turner IV, Rhett Turner, Beauregard Turner and Jennie Turner.
They have largely pursued their own careers in fields such as business, media and philanthropy, while maintaining relatively private lives compared to their father’s public persona.
Atlanta Braves owner Ted Turner leans to kiss his wife, Jane Fonda, during the World Series game in Atlanta on October 17, 1992. (AP Photo/John Swart)

## What Was Ted Turner's Significance?
Turner’s legacy lies in how he reshaped both media and sports. He founded CNN in 1980, pioneering the 24-hour news model that transformed how audiences consume information. His development of the TBS “superstation” concept also helped create a new model for national television distribution.
Beyond broadcasting, Turner reimagined sports marketing by turning the Atlanta Braves into a national brand and expanding the team’s reach across the country.
He was also a major philanthropist and environmental advocate, committing vast resources to conservation and global initiatives. Taken together, his influence stretched across industries—making him one of the most consequential figures in late 20th-century media.

## What Was Ted Turner's Net Worth?
At the time of his death, Turner’s net worth was estimated at roughly $2.2 billion to $2.8 billion, according to multiple reports. The figure reflects both his success in building a media empire and his extensive philanthropic giving later in life.
His wealth had once been significantly higher—reaching as high as $10 billion in the 1990s—but declined following major media mergers and large-scale donations. Even so, Turner remained a powerful figure financially, with holdings that included vast land assets across the United States.

## Ted Turner and Marlo Hampton's Relationship Debunked
_Real Housewives of Atlanta_ star Marlo Hampton was rumored to be linked to Turner—talk that has been denied by Hampton numerous times.
Rumors started spreading online after Hampton appeared on _The Wendy Williams Show_ in 2019. In the interview, she said she did date a billionaire that ran in Turner's circle, but "never in her life dated Ted Turner." Her rejection was missed from online discourse.
Later, she appeared on Bravo's _Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen_ and during a question about her profession, she mentioned her relationship with the unnamed billionaire, once again rejecting any connection to Turner.
"My grandmother taught me at a young age how to invest in property," Hampton told Cohen. "I've owned properties for years. I also dated a billionaire, I told you before. ... Who was not Ted Turner."

# What to Know About Ted Turner's 3 Ex-Wives, Including Actress Jane Fonda
### NEED TO KNOW
*   CNN founder Ted Turner was married three times to Julia Nye, Jane Shirley Smith and actress Jane Fonda  
*   He welcomed two children with Nye and three children with Smith  
*   Turner died on May 6 at age 87
Ted Turner, who died at age 87 on May 6, was married three times during his life.
The CNN founder wed Julia Gale Nye in 1960. The couple went on to welcome two children, daughter Laura and son Robert "Teddy" Edward IV,before divorcing after just a few years of marriage.
In 1964, Turner married Jane Shirley Smith. The pair, who eventually split in 1988, welcomed three children, Beau, Rhett and Jennie.
The media mogul's final marriage was to actress Jane Fonda from 1991 to 2001. During an interview with Piers Morgan in 2012, Turner admitted that Fonda was "probably" the great love of his life.
"When you love somebody, and you really love them, you never stop loving them," the media mogul added. "There's nothing wrong with that. That's good."
Here's everything to know about Ted Turner's ex-wives: Julia Gale Nye, Jane Shirley Smith and Jane Fonda.

# What to Know About Ted Turner's 3 Ex-Wives, Including Actress Jane Fonda
## Julia Gale Nye
Ted Turner.  
Bettmann/Getty
Julia Gale Nye, the daughter of world champion sailor Harry Gale Nye Jr., met Ted Turner while he was attending Brown University in 1959. The couple married at St. Chrysostom’s Episcopal Church in Chicago on June 22, 1960, according to the _Chicago Tribune_.
They later welcomed a daughter, Laura, in 1961, and a son, Robert Edward IV, in 1963, before going their separate ways, per Michael O'Connor's book _Ted Turner: A Biography_.

# What to Know About Ted Turner's 3 Ex-Wives, Including Actress Jane Fonda
## Jane Shirley Smith
Ted Turner attends official CNN Launch event on June 01, 1980 in Atlanta, Georgia.  
Rick Diamond/Getty
Shortly after his divorce from Nye, Turner married Jane Shirley Smith on June 2, 1964. Smith, a Delta Air Lines flight attendant, reportedly met Turner at a Young Republicans meeting.
The couple welcomed three children together: son Rhett in 1965 — named after Rhett Butler from _Gone with the Wind_ — followed by son Beau in 1968 and daughter Sarah Jean “Jennie” in 1969.
Turner and Smith divorced in 1988.

texts.0:
Ted Turner, the billionaire media mogul who founded CNN and helped reshape modern television, died Wednesday, at age 87.
Over decades, Turner built a vast empire that included cable networks such as TBS and TNT, while also leaving a lasting mark on professional sports through his ownership of the Atlanta Braves.
Known for his bold personality and willingness to take risks, he transformed both the way news is delivered—launching the first 24-hour cable news channel—and how sports teams could be marketed to a national audience. His larger-than-life persona, as well as his marriages to high-profile figures including actor Jane Fonda, cemented his place as one of the most recognizable media figures of his era.
texts.1:
#### Read More on U.S.
He was married three times throughout his life—to Julia Gale Nye, Jane Shirley Smith and Jane Fonda—and had five children across those relationships.
Jane Fonda peers out from under a towel shielding her from the rain as she and her husband, Ted Turner, watch the Atlanta Braves defeat the Pittsburgh...
Fonda paid tribute to Turner with a deeply personal reflection, describing him as a transformative presence in her life who brought both passion and support.
In a statement, Fonda recalled how Turner “swept into my life, a gloriously handsome, deeply romantic” figure whose larger-than-life persona was matched by his accomplishments as the founder of CNN and Turner Classic Movies and his success as a world-class sailor.
Fonda said he “could see around corners” and credited him with teaching her about wildlife conservation, as well as broader lessons in business and life. His competitive nature, she added, was among his defining traits, comparing it to that of legendary actor Katharine Hepburn.
She also pointed to Turner’s influence beyond his personal relationships, recalling how he challenged those around him to “think big and act small,” including encouraging ambitious ideas like banning nuclear weapons while embracing everyday acts such as picking up trash.
Fonda reflected on Turner’s environmental legacy, saying she imagines him reunited “with all the wildlife he helped bring back from extinction,” including bison, wolves and other species. She also acknowledged his five children, describing them as “talented, complex” individuals and noting the challenges and pride that came with being part of his extended family.
“I loved Ted with all my heart,” Fonda said, closing her tribute by honoring his lasting impact and memory: “You are loved and you will be remembered.”
texts.2:
## Ted Turner's First Wife, Julia Gale Nye
Turner married his first wife, Nye, in 1960. The marriage ended in divorce in 1964. Together, they had two children.
Nye largely stayed out of the public spotlight, even as Turner’s media career accelerated in the following decades. The relationship came during his early years in business, before he built the broadcasting empire that would later make him a household name.
texts.3:
## Ted Turner's Second Wife, Jane Shirley Smith
Turner married Smith in 1965, beginning a relationship that would last more than two decades. The couple divorced in 1988.
They had three children together. During this period, Turner was expanding his television holdings and taking increasingly high-profile risks across sports and media, including acquiring the Atlanta Braves and building out his cable networks.
Ted Turner and Jane Fonda are shown in this 1990 file photo. (AP Images)
texts.4:
## Ted Turner and Jane Fonda: What We Know
Turner’s most high-profile marriage was to actor and activist Fonda, whom he married in 1991. The relationship drew widespread attention given their celebrity status and influence in different fields, with the pairing bringing together two of the most recognizable public figures of the era.
The couple remained married for about a decade before divorcing in 2001, and they did not have children together. Their relationship played out largely in the public eye during a period when Turner’s media empire was expanding and Fonda was continuing her work in film and activism, keeping both figures firmly in the spotlight.
Their marriage also reflected a broader mix of personalities and priorities that defined both of their careers. Turner, known for his outspoken and often unpredictable style, contrasted with Fonda’s evolving focus on activism and spirituality, dynamics that were often noted in coverage of their relationship.
Even after their divorce, the relationship remained a defining part of Turner’s personal life. He later spoke publicly about the significance of the marriage, describing Fonda as one of the most important relationships he had—underscoring how closely his personal life and public profile were intertwined during that period.
texts.5:
## Ted Turner's Kids
Turner had five children across his first two marriages: Laura Turner Seydel, Robert Edward Turner IV, Rhett Turner, Beauregard Turner and Jennie Turner.
They have largely pursued their own careers in fields such as business, media and philanthropy, while maintaining relatively private lives compared to their father’s public persona.
Atlanta Braves owner Ted Turner leans to kiss his wife, Jane Fonda, during the World Series game in Atlanta on October 17, 1992. (AP Photo/John Swart)
texts.6:
## What Was Ted Turner's Significance?
Turner’s legacy lies in how he reshaped both media and sports. He founded CNN in 1980, pioneering the 24-hour news model that transformed how audiences consume information. His development of the TBS “superstation” concept also helped create a new model for national television distribution.
Beyond broadcasting, Turner reimagined sports marketing by turning the Atlanta Braves into a national brand and expanding the team’s reach across the country.
He was also a major philanthropist and environmental advocate, committing vast resources to conservation and global initiatives. Taken together, his influence stretched across industries—making him one of the most consequential figures in late 20th-century media.
texts.7:
## What Was Ted Turner's Net Worth?
At the time of his death, Turner’s net worth was estimated at roughly $2.2 billion to $2.8 billion, according to multiple reports. The figure reflects both his success in building a media empire and his extensive philanthropic giving later in life.
His wealth had once been significantly higher—reaching as high as $10 billion in the 1990s—but declined following major media mergers and large-scale donations. Even so, Turner remained a powerful figure financially, with holdings that included vast land assets across the United States.
texts.8:
## Ted Turner and Marlo Hampton's Relationship Debunked
_Real Housewives of Atlanta_ star Marlo Hampton was rumored to be linked to Turner—talk that has been denied by Hampton numerous times.
Rumors started spreading online after Hampton appeared on _The Wendy Williams Show_ in 2019. In the interview, she said she did date a billionaire that ran in Turner's circle, but "never in her life dated Ted Turner." Her rejection was missed from online discourse.
Later, she appeared on Bravo's _Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen_ and during a question about her profession, she mentioned her relationship with the unnamed billionaire, once again rejecting any connection to Turner.
"My grandmother taught me at a young age how to invest in property," Hampton told Cohen. "I've owned properties for years. I also dated a billionaire, I told you before. ... Who was not Ted Turner."
